content: Butz-Choquin is a French pipe manufacturer that was established in 1858 by tobacconist Jean-Baptiste Choquin and Gustave Butz. The company was originally founded in Metz, where it remained until 1951. In that year, it was purchased by the Berrod-Regad company and subsequently relocated to Saint-Claude, Jura. In 1960, Butz-Choquin began exporting its pipes internationally, earning prestigious accolades such as the Oscar of Export and the Gold Cup of the French Good Taste. In 2002, the company was acquired by Fabien Guichon. The first pipe produced by Butz-Choquin, known as the Choquin pipe, was a curved pipe featuring a flat-bottomed hearth, albatross bone, and silver rings. Today, the company manufactures over 70 distinct series of pipes. Notably, Butz-Choquin pipes have only been widely available in the United States since 1999.
